claims.text: Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 is a dual-nanoprecipitation high-entropy alloy.
The alloy was produced by additive manufacturing.
The additively manufactured alloy has enhanced strength relative to cast and wrought versions.
An ETEM equipped with in-situ heating and EDS/EELS can be used to examine oxidation and elemental redistribution in the alloy in real time.
Oxidation at 800–1000 °C under controlled oxygen pressure can simulate relevant gas-turbine or aerospace service conditions.
High-temperature oxidation and corrosion degrade gas-turbine components.
HEAs are of interest for high-temperature aerospace, power-generation, and gas-turbine applications.
During high-temperature oxidation, nanoprecipitates in the additively manufactured alloy undergo real-time elemental redistribution.
Elemental redistribution at nanoprecipitates directly correlates with localized oxide-layer formation and growth kinetics.
Nanoprecipitates and their evolving elemental compositions mediate oxide-phase formation and growth.
Elevated temperature causes differential oxidation rates among the alloy's constituent elements.
Differential oxidation selectively enriches or depletes particular elements at nanoprecipitates.
Elemental segregation at nanoprecipitates modulates oxide nucleation and growth and thereby affects local oxidation kinetics.
In-situ ETEM will reveal elemental redistribution concurrent with the initiation and progression of oxide-layer formation.
Regions enriched in Ti or Cr will exhibit slower oxide growth than less-protected regions.
Ti and Cr are oxidation-resistant elements in the relevant alloy and conditions.
Ex-situ post-oxidation analyses have shown overall oxidation degradation but cannot capture transient nanoscale elemental redistribution.
Electron-transparent ETEM samples can be heated incrementally to 1000 °C in oxygen while continuously collecting high-resolution images and elemental maps.
